title: Advanced Optional Exercise Plan C — Yoga Intensive for Diabetes Reversal
body: Daily, 60 minutes. Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation): 20 rounds. Standing asanas (60-90s each): Trikonasana, Virabhadrasana I & II, Ardha Chandrasana, Utkatasana. Seated asanas: Paschimottanasana, Janu Sirsasana, Ardha Matsyendrasana (both sides), Baddha Konasana. Supine asanas: Setu Bandhasana, Halasana, Sarvangasana (if safe). Prone asanas: Bhujangasana, Dhanurasana, Shalabhasana. Core asanas: Navasana, Plank, Side plank. Pranayama: Kapalbhati 5 min, Anulom Vilom 10 min, Bhramari 5 min. Meditation 10 min. Shavasana 10 min.

title: Condition-Specific Dietary Modifications — Diabetic Kidney Disease
body:
Restrict: protein to 0.6-0.8g/kg body weight; sodium under 2g/day; potassium-rich foods if potassium is elevated (bananas, tomatoes, potatoes, oranges); phosphorus-rich foods (dairy, nuts, beans) if phosphorus is elevated.

Include: high-quality protein sources (egg whites, limited paneer, limited dal); low-potassium vegetables (cabbage, cucumber, bottle gourd, ridge gourd); adequate hydration unless fluid restriction is advised.

title: Condition-Specific Dietary Modifications — Diabetic Retinopathy
body:
Include: high-antioxidant foods (blueberries, spinach, kale, carrots, bell peppers); lutein and zeaxanthin sources (spinach, kale, egg yolks); omega-3-rich foods (flaxseeds, walnuts, chia seeds); Vitamin A sources (carrots, sweet potatoes, spinach).

Supplements: Lutein 10mg daily; Zeaxanthin 2mg daily; Bilberry extract 160mg twice daily; Vitamin A 3000 IU daily (if not pregnant).

title: Condition-Specific Dietary Modifications — Diabetic Neuropathy
body: Include: B-vitamin-rich foods (whole grains, eggs, legumes, green leafy vegetables); antioxidant-rich foods (berries, 85%+ dark chocolate, green tea); anti-inflammatory foods (turmeric, ginger, fatty fish if non-vegetarian).

title: Condition-Specific Dietary Modifications — Fatty Liver
body:
Avoid completely: all fried foods, all refined oils, all processed/packaged foods, alcohol, high-fructose foods and beverages.

Include: cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, cabbage — support liver detox pathways); beetroot (powerful liver detoxifier); garlic and onions (sulfur compounds support Phase 2 liver detox); green tea (antioxidants support liver health); bitter gourd and bitter greens.

title: Troubleshooting — What to Do If You Are Not Seeing Results
body:
Blood sugar not dropping fast enough: increase the morning fasted walk to 90 minutes; extend post-meal walks to 30 minutes; reduce grain portions further (1/4 cup at lunch, zero at dinner); add Gymnema Sylvestre 500mg before each meal; increase bitter melon juice to 50ml daily; double-check medication timing/adherence and hidden sugars in food; increase water to 5 litres; add apple cider vinegar before meals.

Low blood sugar episodes (hypoglycemia): consume 15g fast-acting carbs immediately (3-4 glucose tablets, 1 tbsp honey, or 1/2 cup fruit juice), sit/lie down, recheck after 15 minutes and repeat if still low. Contact your doctor immediately for a medication dose review — do not skip meals, carry glucose tablets always, and monitor blood sugar 6-8 times daily until stable.

Extreme fatigue or weakness: check calorie intake is adequate (min. 1200-1500 kcal for women, 1500-1800 for men); get iron, B12, Vitamin D and thyroid labs checked; add Ashwagandha 600mg twice daily, CoQ10 200mg daily, L-Carnitine 1000mg daily; ensure 1g/kg protein and 7-8 hours sleep; temporarily reduce exercise intensity; add Chyawanprash 2 tsp daily.

Constipation: increase water to 4-5 litres; increase fiber (isabgol, flaxseeds, vegetables); Triphala 1 tsp twice daily; isabgol 1 tsp in warm water before bed; include prunes, figs, papaya; increase movement; practice abdominal massage and Pawanmuktasana (Wind-Relieving Pose).

Sleep issues persisting: increase evening Ashwagandha to 600mg; add Brahmi+Jatamansi, Magnesium Glycinate 500mg, L-Theanine 200mg before bed; consider Melatonin 0.5-1mg (start low); practice Yoga Nidra; ensure complete darkness and a cool room (65-68 F); no screens after 9 PM; nightly foot oil massage (non-negotiable).

Joint pain or muscle soreness increasing: temporarily reduce exercise intensity and increase rest; add Curcumin 1000mg twice daily, Boswellia 500mg twice daily, Yogaraj Guggulu 500mg three times daily; warm oil massage on painful joints (10 min, leave 30 min before showering); Epsom salt bath 3x/week; ensure adequate protein and sleep; add collagen 10g daily; gentle daily yoga/stretching.

Not losing weight: check portion sizes and hidden calories (oil, ghee, nuts); increase exercise intensity/duration and add strength training; raise protein to 1.2-1.5g/kg; try 18:6 fasting if safe; add apple cider vinegar before meals; check thyroid and cortisol; ensure adequate sleep; add green coffee bean extract, L-Carnitine before exercise, green tea 3x daily.

Increased hunger or cravings: increase protein and fiber at each meal; drink 2 glasses of water before assuming you are hungry (thirst is often mistaken for hunger); add Gymnema Sylvestre 500mg (kills sweet cravings); ensure adequate sleep and manage stress; drink herbal tea when cravings hit and wait 10 minutes (it passes); check if any medication (insulin, sulfonylureas) is increasing appetite.

title: Important Safety Reminders — Read Before Following This Plan
body:
If you are on insulin or sulfonylureas: monitor blood sugar 6-8 times daily; contact your doctor immediately if blood sugar repeatedly drops below 80 mg/dL — a medication dose reduction will likely be needed within 3-7 days of starting this plan.

If you have severe kidney disease (Stage 4-5): do not follow this plan without nephrologist approval — protein and potassium restrictions may be needed.

If you have severe heart disease: consult your cardiologist before starting intensive exercise; start low-intensity and increase gradually.

If you have active diabetic foot ulcers: avoid prolonged walking, focus on upper-body and seated exercises, and seek immediate medical treatment for the ulcer.

If you are pregnant or breastfeeding: do not follow this plan — consult your OB/GYN and endocrinologist for safe diabetes management.

Medication interactions: tell your doctor about every herb and supplement you take. Some interact with medications — Sarpagandha with BP medications, Guggul with thyroid medications, and blood-thinning herbs (garlic, ginger, high-dose turmeric) with anticoagulants.

Stop the plan and seek immediate medical help for: severe chest pain/pressure, severe difficulty breathing, sudden vision loss, severe abdominal pain, blood in urine or stool, blood sugar persistently below 60 mg/dL, severe dizziness/fainting, confusion, or any symptom that feels life-threatening.

Medical supervision is required before starting if you have: active heart disease, a recent heart attack, angina or cardiac stents; severe kidney disease (eGFR below 30); severe retinopathy with bleeding risk; active diabetic foot ulcers; uncontrolled BP above 180/110; pregnancy or breastfeeding; recent surgery (within 3 months); or active cancer/chemotherapy.

title: Vitamin D — The Insulin Hormone Regulator
body:
A prohormone that directly controls insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity, inflammation and immune function — 80% of diabetics are deficient. Correcting it raises insulin sensitivity by up to 60%, cuts HbA1c by 0.5-1.2%, and lowers cardiovascular risk by 43%.

Sources: 15-20 min sunlight daily (7-9 AM or 4-6 PM, arms+legs exposed, no sunscreen); wild salmon 600-1000 IU/100g, mackerel 360, sardines 480; egg yolks 87 IU each (2-3/day); UV-exposed mushrooms 400-1600 IU/100g; fortified almond milk 100 IU/cup; grass-fed ghee/butter.

Daily target: 2000-4000 IU (5000-10,000 IU for 8-12 weeks if severely deficient, doctor supervised). Best taken with a fat-containing meal, morning/afternoon. Test 25-OH Vitamin D — target 40-60 ng/mL, retest every 3 months.

title: Vitamin B12 — The Nerve Protector
body:
Essential for nerve health, red blood cells, DNA synthesis and energy. Metformin depletes B12 by up to 30% within 2 years — anyone on it 2+ years, vegetarians/vegans, the elderly, Type 1 diabetics, and anyone with gut inflammation is most at risk.

Repairs damaged nerves and prevents/reduces diabetic neuropathy (tingling, numbness, burning), improves energy and cognition, prevents anemia.

Sources: eggs 1.1mcg each; plain yogurt 1.4mcg/cup, paneer 0.9mcg/100g; clams 84mcg/100g (highest in nature), oysters 16mcg/100g; salmon 4.8mcg/100g; beef liver 70mcg/100g; nutritional yeast 8-24mcg/2 tbsp (best vegetarian source).

Daily target: 500-1000mcg (1000-2000mcg therapeutic for neuropathy) — sublingual or methylcobalamin form absorbs best. Take in the morning. Test serum B12 (>400 pg/mL, optimal >600) and homocysteine (<10 µmol/L).

title: Vitamin C — The Blood Sugar Stabiliser
body:
Lowers post-meal blood sugar spikes by up to 30%, cuts HbA1c by 0.5% over 12 weeks, speeds wound healing, strengthens blood vessels (protects against retinopathy/nephropathy), and lowers diabetic complication risk by 35%.

Sources: red bell pepper 190mg/cup raw; guava 377mg/cup (highest); kiwi 137mg/cup; strawberries 89mg/cup; broccoli 81mg/cup cooked; oranges 70mg each.

Daily target: 500-1000mg, split into 2 doses (max 2000mg/day). Take morning and afternoon, with meals. Don't overcook vegetables — Vitamin C degrades with heat; steam or eat raw. Avoid high doses if prone to kidney stones.

title: Vitamin E — The Cellular Protector
body:
A fat-soluble antioxidant that protects pancreatic beta cells, improves insulin sensitivity, protects eyes/kidneys/nerves, and reduces LDL oxidation. Cuts HbA1c by 0.4-0.8% over 3-6 months and lowers diabetic retinopathy risk by 40%.

Sources: almonds 7.3mg/oz (23 almonds); sunflower seeds 7.4mg/oz; avocado 4mg each; spinach 3.7mg/cup cooked; wheat germ oil 20mg/tbsp (highest).

Daily target: 15-30mg (therapeutic 400-800 IU for complications, consult doctor). Take with a fat-containing meal. Choose natural d-alpha-tocopherol over synthetic dl-alpha-tocopherol; avoid mega-doses without supervision (bleeding risk); works best paired with Vitamin C and Selenium.

title: Magnesium — The Insulin Sensitivity Mineral
body:
Involved in 300+ enzyme reactions including insulin secretion, ATP production and blood pressure regulation. ~70% of diabetics are deficient — high blood sugar makes the kidneys excrete 300% more magnesium.

Reverses insulin resistance at the cellular level, lowers fasting sugar 10-20%, cuts HbA1c 0.5-1.0%, lowers BP 5-10mmHg, prevents cramps, improves sleep.

Sources: pumpkin seeds 168mg/oz; spinach 157mg/cup cooked; black beans 120mg/cup; almonds 80mg/oz; 85%+ dark chocolate 64mg/oz; quinoa 118mg/cup.

Daily target: 400-600mg (glycinate or citrate form). Take in the evening with food (promotes relaxation/sleep). Test RBC magnesium (not serum) — target >5.5mg/dL.

title: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) — The Energy Producer
body:
Fuels cellular energy and glucose metabolism. Diabetic thiamine levels are often 75% lower than normal, driving fatigue, neuropathy and diabetic cardiomyopathy.

Prevents/reverses neuropathy (especially in the feet), improves energy, protects the heart, enhances glucose metabolism.

Sources: pork 0.8mg/100g; lentils 0.33mg/cup; brown rice 0.4mg/cup; sunflower seeds 0.4mg/oz; macadamia or pistachio 0.7mg/cup.

Standard RDA (1.2-1.5mg) is far too low for diabetics — therapeutic dose is 50-100mg, or Benfotiamine (fat-soluble, superior for diabetic complications) 300-600mg for neuropathy. Take in the morning with meals.

title: Vitamin K2 — The Arterial Cleanser
body:
The "calcium traffic director" — pulls calcium out of arteries and directs it into bone, cutting cardiovascular events by 52% and improving bone density, with a 26% lower all-cause mortality in studies.

Sources: natto (fermented soybeans) 1085mcg/100g — highest in nature, 1 tbsp/day is enough; gouda 75mcg/100g; pasture-raised egg yolks 32mcg each; grass-fed ghee 12mcg/tsp; chicken thigh 9mcg/100g.

Daily target: 100-200mcg (MK-7 form; therapeutic 180-360mcg). Take with a fat-containing meal. Always pair with Vitamin D3 (synergistic). Avoid if on Warfarin/blood thinners without medical supervision.

title: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine) — The Blood Sugar Stabiliser
body:
Regulates blood sugar metabolism, supports neurotransmitter production, helps prevent diabetic neuropathy (especially with B12), and lowers homocysteine (cardiovascular risk marker).

Sources: chickpeas 1.1mg/cup cooked; chicken breast 1.0mg/100g; tuna 1.0mg/100g; less-ripe banana 0.4mg; avocado 0.4mg each; sweet potato 0.6mg.

Standard RDA (1.3-1.7mg) is insufficient for diabetics — therapeutic dose is 25-50mg/day. Do not exceed 100mg/day long-term (very high doses can cause nerve damage). Take morning/afternoon with food; works best combined with B12 and Folate.

title: Biotin (Vitamin B7) — The Metabolic Enhancer
body:
Works alongside insulin to enhance glucose, fat and protein metabolism, and supports skin/hair/nails (often affected in diabetics). High doses can lower fasting glucose by 18-45% and improve insulin sensitivity and neuropathy symptoms.

Sources: eggs 10mcg each (in the yolk); walnuts 9.5mcg/oz; boiled sweet potato 2.4mcg; soybeans 8.7mcg/cup; salmon 5mcg/100g.

Daily target: 30-100mcg for general health; 5,000-10,000mcg (5-10mg) therapeutic for blood sugar control, doctor supervised. Take in the morning with breakfast. Caution: doses above 300mcg/day can distort thyroid/cardiac lab tests — tell your doctor before any blood work. Works well with chromium and alpha-lipoic acid.

title: Folate (Vitamin B9) — The Cardiovascular Protector
body:
Supports DNA repair, red blood cell production, and lowers homocysteine — a major cardiovascular risk factor. Cuts cardiovascular complications by ~40% and lowers diabetic nephropathy risk.

Sources: lentils 358mcg/cup cooked (highest); spinach 263mcg/cup cooked; chickpeas 282mcg/cup; asparagus 268mcg/cup cooked; avocado 163mcg each; methi (fenugreek) leaves 84mcg/cup.

Daily target: 400-800mcg (therapeutic 1000-5000mcg as methylfolate). Take in the morning with food. Use methylfolate (5-MTHF) — about 40% of people can't properly convert synthetic "folic acid." Always pair with B12 and B6; test homocysteine (<10 µmol/L); don't mega-dose folate without checking B12 first, since high folate can mask a B12 deficiency.

title: Chromium — The Insulin Amplifier
body:
Enhances insulin receptor sensitivity and glucose metabolism, and cuts sugar cravings — 73% of diabetics are deficient. Improves insulin sensitivity by up to 50%, lowers fasting sugar 10-30 mg/dL, cuts HbA1c 0.6-1.0%, and reduces sugar/carb cravings by ~70%.

Sources: broccoli 11mcg/½ cup cooked (highest); grapes 8mcg/cup; barley 13mcg/cup; brewer's yeast 60mcg/tbsp (richest supplemental source); black pepper 10mcg/tbsp.

Daily target: 200-400mcg (chromium picolinate; therapeutic 400-1000mcg for diabetes). Take with carb-containing meals, morning and evening. Hard to lab-test directly — track response via fasting glucose and HbA1c instead.

title: Zinc — The Insulin Storage Mineral
body:
Essential for insulin synthesis, storage and secretion, plus immunity, wound healing and thyroid/testosterone function — 48% of diabetics are deficient. Lowers fasting sugar ~12%, speeds wound healing, and cuts infection risk by ~50%.

Sources: oysters 74mg/100g (highest); pumpkin seeds 7.8mg/oz (best plant source); beef 7mg/100g; chickpeas/lentils ~2.5mg/cup; cheddar 3.1mg/100g.

Daily target: 15-30mg elemental zinc (therapeutic 30-50mg short-term for deficiency). Take in the evening with food, not alongside calcium or iron. Best forms: zinc picolinate, citrate, or gluconate. Don't exceed 40mg/day long-term — it causes copper deficiency; keep a 10:1 zinc:copper ratio.

title: Selenium — The Thyroid & Immune Protector
body:
Converts thyroid hormone T4 to active T3, and is a powerful antioxidant — diabetics with thyroid issues are almost always selenium deficient. Protects beta cells, lowers CRP by 23%, improves insulin sensitivity, and lowers thyroid antibodies.

Sources: Brazil nuts 544mcg/oz — highest food source, 2-3 nuts/day is enough (more risks toxicity); yellowfin tuna 92mcg/100g; sardines 53mcg/100g; beef/turkey ~30mcg/100g; eggs 15mcg each.

Daily target: 100-200mcg (therapeutic 200-400mcg for thyroid support). Take in the morning with food; selenomethionine is the best-absorbed form. Do not exceed 400mcg/day. Works synergistically with Vitamin E and iodine.

title: Potassium — The Blood Pressure & Insulin Regulator
body:
Needed for insulin secretion from beta cells, blood pressure regulation and heart rhythm — low potassium directly impairs insulin secretion. Lowers BP 5-10mmHg and stroke risk by 24%.

Sources: avocado 975mg each (more than 2 bananas); beet greens 1309mg/cup (highest); white beans 1189mg/cup; baked potato with skin 926mg; spinach 839mg/cup cooked; tomato paste 1065mg/½ cup; coconut water 600mg/cup.

Daily target: 3000-4700mg — get this from FOOD, not supplements. Do not self-supplement potassium — it can cause dangerous heart rhythms, especially if you're on ACE inhibitors or ARBs for blood pressure; consult your doctor first. Test serum potassium, target 4.0-5.0 mEq/L.

title: Calcium — The Metabolic Signal Regulator
body:
Needed for insulin secretion signalling, bone health (diabetics have higher fracture risk), and blood vessel function.

Sources: plain yogurt 448mg/cup; fortified almond milk 450mg/cup; calcium-set tofu 434mg/½ cup; sardines 325mg/100g; paneer 200mg/100g; collard greens 268mg/cup cooked.

Daily target: 1000-1200mg (1200-1500mg if bone health is a concern), split into ~500mg doses for better absorption. Calcium citrate can be taken any time; calcium carbonate needs food. An evening dose supports sleep and bone remodeling. Always pair with Vitamin D3 and K2; don't exceed 2500mg/day; don't take alongside iron or zinc. Test serum calcium, target 8.5-10.5 mg/dL.

title: Iron — The Oxygen Transport Mineral
body:
Needed for oxygen transport (hemoglobin), energy production, immunity and thyroid hormone synthesis. Deficiency causes the severe fatigue common in diabetics.

Heme sources (best absorbed): chicken liver 11mg/100g, beef liver 5.2mg/100g, oysters 5.7mg/100g. Plant (non-heme, lower absorption): lentils 6.6mg/cup cooked, tofu 6.6mg/½ cup, spinach 6.4mg/cup cooked.

Daily target: 8mg (men), 18mg (premenopausal women), 8mg (postmenopausal women); if deficient, 50-100mg ferrous bisglycinate. Take on an empty stomach for best absorption (small food if it causes nausea); avoid taking with coffee, tea, dairy, calcium or zinc; pair with Vitamin C (+300% absorption). Do NOT supplement without testing first — excess iron is toxic. Test serum ferritin, target 50-100 ng/mL, plus hemoglobin.

title: Manganese — The Glucose Metabolism Cofactor
body:
Supports glucose metabolism, antioxidant defense, bone formation and wound healing — deficiency worsens glucose intolerance.

Sources: pine nuts 8.8mg/cup (highest); pineapple 2.6mg/cup (highest fruit source); oats 3.7mg/cup; chickpeas 1.7mg/cup; cloves 30mg/tbsp.

Daily target: 2-5mg (therapeutic 5-10mg); don't exceed 11mg/day (toxicity risk). Take with meals. Usually sufficient from diet alone — supplementation is rarely needed, and high iron intake can reduce manganese absorption.

title: Copper — The Cardiovascular & Energy Mineral
body:
Supports iron metabolism, energy production, antioxidant defense, and blood vessel/connective tissue health.

Sources: beef liver 14.3mg/100g (very high); oysters 7.6mg/100g; cashews 0.6mg/oz; chickpeas 0.6mg/cup; dark chocolate 0.5mg/oz.

Daily target: 0.9-2mg, usually sufficient from diet. Balance it 10:1 with zinc — if taking more than 50mg/day of zinc, add ~2mg copper. Don't exceed 10mg/day.

title: Phosphorus — The Energy & Bone Mineral
body:
Needed for ATP (cellular energy), bone/teeth formation, DNA/RNA synthesis and kidney function.

Sources: pumpkin seeds 1233mg/cup (highest); sunflower seeds 1158mg/cup; sardines 490mg/100g; mozzarella 415mg/100g; salmon 371mg/100g; lentils 356mg/cup.

Daily target: 700-1250mg, usually sufficient from diet — supplementation is rarely needed. Keep it roughly balanced 1:1 with calcium, and avoid high-phosphorus processed foods and soft drinks, which can leach calcium from bone.

title: Iodine — The Thyroid Function Mineral
body:
Needed for thyroid hormone production (T3/T4), metabolism and brain function. 30-40% of diabetics have thyroid dysfunction, often worsened by iodine deficiency.

Sources: iodised salt 71mcg/¼ tsp; yogurt 75mcg/cup; cod 99mcg/100g; egg 24mcg each; kelp 2000mcg/g (use cautiously — very high).

Daily target: 150mcg general health, 200-300mcg if thyroid support is needed; don't exceed 1100mcg/day. Take in the morning with food. If you have Hashimoto's thyroiditis, consult your doctor before supplementing — it can worsen autoimmunity. Always pair with selenium. Test TSH, Free T3, Free T4, and urinary iodine.

title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA) — The Universal Antioxidant
body:
A powerful antioxidant that works in both water and fat, crossing every cell membrane, and regenerates Vitamin C, E and glutathione. The #1 supplement for diabetic neuropathy, backed by 15+ clinical trials.

Cuts nerve pain by 60% within 3-5 weeks, improves nerve conduction and reverses tingling/numbness; improves insulin sensitivity by up to 50%, lowers fasting sugar 10-30%, cuts HbA1c 0.5-1.0%; lowers liver enzymes (helps fatty liver); improves blood vessel (endothelial) function.

Dose: 600mg/day standard (600mg twice daily/1200mg total for severe neuropathy) — start at 300mg and increase gradually. Take on an empty stomach, 30 minutes before meals (food cuts absorption by ~30%). Best form: R-Lipoic Acid (R-ALA), more potent than the standard mixed form. Caution: monitor blood sugar closely (can lower it significantly); may deplete biotin (pair with 300mcg biotin); can cause mild nausea at first.

title: Berberine — The Natural Metformin Alternative
body:
Activates the same AMPK pathway as Metformin, with extra benefits for cholesterol, fatty liver and gut health.

Lowers fasting sugar 15-25% (comparable to Metformin), cuts HbA1c 0.7-2.0% in 3 months, improves insulin sensitivity by up to 45%; lowers LDL 20-25%, total cholesterol 18%, triglycerides 23-35%, and raises HDL; reduces liver fat by 52% in 16 weeks; supports modest weight loss (~5 lbs/12 weeks) and a healthier gut microbiome.

Dose: 500mg, 3 times daily (1500mg total) before meals — start with 500mg once daily and increase over 1-2 weeks. Best form: Berberine HCl (most studied) or Dihydroberberine (200mg ≈ 500mg regular berberine). Caution: GI upset (diarrhea, cramping, gas) in the first 1-2 weeks — start low; avoid in pregnancy/breastfeeding; can interact with antibiotics and other medications (CYP450 enzymes) — consult your doctor if on multiple medications; monitor blood sugar closely if also on diabetes medication (effects can stack).

title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA) — The Anti-Inflammatory Essential Fat
body:
Diabetics carry 3x the cardiovascular risk and chronic inflammation of non-diabetics — omega-3s address both. Lowers triglycerides 25-30%, BP 5-10mmHg, heart attack risk 45%, and CRP by up to 30%; improves insulin sensitivity; protects nerves (less neuropathic pain); cuts liver fat 30-50%; supports mood and cognition.

Dose: 2000-3000mg combined EPA+DHA/day (3000-4000mg if triglycerides are high), EPA:DHA ratio of 2:1 or 3:2. Take with meals (fat-soluble). Best form: triglyceride or re-esterified triglyceride (rTG) — avoid the poorly-absorbed ethyl ester form.

Sources: mackerel 4580mg/100g (highest), salmon 2200mg/100g, sardines 1480mg/100g, herring 2150mg/100g — 3-4 servings/week. Plant ALA (flax, chia, walnut) only converts 5-10% to EPA/DHA, so direct sources are preferred.

Caution: choose molecularly-distilled, third-party-tested brands (heavy metals/PCBs) with IFOS certification, keep refrigerated, and note it may raise bleeding risk on blood thinners.

title: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) — The Cellular Energy Booster
body:
A key mitochondrial-energy antioxidant that statin medications (commonly prescribed to diabetics with high cholesterol) deplete by 40-50% — and diabetics already run mitochondrial dysfunction (low cellular energy).

Improves insulin sensitivity and lowers fasting sugar 8-15%, cuts HbA1c 0.4-1.0%; improves heart muscle function, lowers BP 10-15mmHg, protects against heart failure; reduces fatigue and improves exercise performance; protects nerves and kidneys from oxidative damage.

Dose: 100-200mg/day general health (200-400mg/day if on statins or for therapeutic effect). Best form: Ubiquinol — the active, reduced form, absorbed ~8x better than standard Ubiquinone (best for people over 40 or with mitochondrial issues). Take with a fat-containing meal (absorption up to 3x higher), morning or early afternoon — take before 2 PM as it can cause mild insomnia if taken late in the day. Essential to take alongside any statin medication; may enhance blood-thinning medications (monitor with your doctor). Very safe overall, with no known serious side effects.

title: Milk Thistle (Silymarin) — The Liver Protector & Regenerator
body:
Contains silymarin, a flavonoid complex that protects and regenerates liver cells — used for over 2000 years. 30-70% of diabetics have fatty liver, which worsens insulin resistance.

Reduces liver fat by up to 50% in 6 months, lowers liver enzymes (ALT/AST) 30-40%, reverses liver inflammation, prevents progression to cirrhosis; also improves insulin sensitivity (fasting sugar -10-15%, HbA1c -0.5-1.0%) and lowers LDL 10-15%.

Dose: 200-400mg silymarin, 3 times daily (600-1200mg total), standardized to 70-80% silymarin — start at 200mg once daily and increase gradually. Take with meals, 3 divided doses. Best form: Silybin phytosome (Siliphos®) — absorbs ~10x better than standard silymarin.

Very safe, used for decades. May cause mild GI upset initially; can interact with liver-metabolized medications (CYP450) — consult your doctor; avoid if allergic to ragweed/daisies/marigolds. Monitor liver enzymes every 3 months; ultrasound/FibroScan to track liver fat.

title: Cinnamon Extract (Ceylon) — The Blood Sugar Stabiliser
body:
Contains MHCP, a compound that mimics insulin action and improves glucose metabolism — one of the most studied natural blood sugar regulators.

Lowers fasting sugar 10-29%, cuts post-meal spikes up to 30%, lowers HbA1c 0.4-0.8% in 3 months; also lowers LDL 10-15% and triglycerides 23-30%, and is a powerful antioxidant.

Dose: 500-2000mg/day standardized extract, or 1-6g/day whole powder (start at 500mg and increase based on response). Take with meals, especially carb-containing ones.

Always choose Ceylon cinnamon (Cinnamomum verum) — Cassia cinnamon is high in coumarin, which can damage the liver in high long-term doses. May enhance blood-thinning medications; monitor blood sugar closely if combined with diabetes medication (hypoglycemia risk). Safe long-term if Ceylon variety. Track fasting/post-meal glucose and HbA1c every 6-8 weeks.

title: Bitter Melon (Karela) Extract — The Natural Insulin Mimicker
body:
A traditional Ayurvedic/Chinese remedy containing plant insulin (polypeptide-p) that mimics human insulin and activates AMPK (same pathway as Metformin/berberine).

Lowers fasting sugar 15-25%, cuts post-meal spikes up to 54%, lowers HbA1c 0.25-1.0%; protects beta cells and may support their regeneration; supports fat metabolism.

Dose: 500-2000mg/day standardized extract, or 50-100mL fresh juice, or ½-1 cup whole cooked bitter melon daily. Take 30 minutes before meals, morning and evening. Best form: standardized extract (10-25:1).

Preparation: stir-fry sliced/deseeded bitter melon with turmeric/cumin/garlic; or blend fresh juice with lemon and ginger to mask bitterness; or steep dried slices as tea.

Very bitter and may cause GI upset in sensitive individuals; can lower blood sugar significantly — monitor closely if on medication; avoid in pregnancy (may cause uterine contractions); start low (500mg) and increase gradually.

title: Gymnema Sylvestre — The "Sugar Destroyer"
body:
Ayurvedic herb ("Gurmar" — destroyer of sugar) that blocks sugar receptors on the tongue and in the intestines, cutting sugar absorption and cravings.

Lowers fasting sugar 20-30%, cuts HbA1c 0.5-1.5% over 6-18 months, blocks intestinal sugar absorption; may regenerate pancreatic beta cells and increase natural insulin secretion up to 2x; blocks sweet-taste receptors, cutting sugar cravings by ~80% in clinical observation.

Dose: 400-600mg/day standardized to 25% gymnemic acids, split into 2 doses, 30-60 minutes before meals — or whenever sugar cravings hit (it blocks the sweet taste for 1-2 hours).

May cause mild nausea initially (start at 200mg); can lower blood sugar significantly — monitor closely if on medication. Very safe, centuries of Ayurvedic use. Track fasting/post-meal glucose, HbA1c every 6-8 weeks, and sugar cravings/dietary compliance.

title: Fenugreek — The Fiber-Rich Glucose Regulator
body:
Fenugreek seeds are 50% soluble fiber (galactomannan) plus 4-hydroxyisoleucine, which together slow glucose absorption and improve insulin secretion.

Lowers fasting sugar 13-25%, cuts post-meal spikes up to 54%, lowers HbA1c 0.4-1.2%, slows gastric emptying; also lowers LDL 14-33%, total cholesterol 14-25%, and triglycerides 25%; high fiber supports gut health and constipation.

Dose: 2.5-15g/day whole seed powder, or 500-1000mg/day standardized extract, or soak 1-2 tbsp seeds overnight (traditional method — drink the water and chew the seeds on an empty stomach in the morning). Take with meals to slow glucose absorption.

Can cause gas/bloating initially — start low; harmlessly gives urine/sweat a maple-syrup smell; may enhance blood-thinning medications; avoid in pregnancy (can stimulate uterine contractions); drink plenty of water. Monitor glucose and lipids every 3 months.

title: N-Acetyl Cysteine (NAC) — The Master Antioxidant Booster
body:
A precursor to glutathione, the body's master antioxidant — diabetics run ~40% lower glutathione due to chronic oxidative stress. Protects liver, kidneys, nerves and blood vessels.

Improves insulin sensitivity up to 30% and lowers fasting sugar 8-15%; protects the liver (lower ALT/AST, less inflammation — helps fatty liver); protects kidneys from diabetic damage; lowers homocysteine and protects against LDL oxidation; supports heavy-metal/toxin detoxification.

Dose: 600-1200mg/day general health, 1200-1800mg/day therapeutic (fatty liver, insulin resistance), split into 2 doses. Take on an empty stomach for best absorption (small food if it causes nausea).

May cause nausea initially — start low; has a normal sulfur smell; pair with Vitamin C (boosts glutathione production further); may loosen stools at first. Very safe — used in hospitals for Tylenol overdose. Monitor liver/kidney function periodically.

title: Enhanced Breakfast: Super Protein Veggie Scramble
body:
3 whole eggs (pasture-raised if possible) + 1 cup spinach + ½ cup bell peppers (red/yellow) + ¼ cup mushrooms (UV-exposed if possible) + 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil + ½ avocado sliced on top + a pinch of turmeric and black pepper + a sprinkle of nutritional yeast (optional).

Method: sauté mushrooms 2 min, add bell peppers 2 min, add spinach until wilted (1 min), pour in scrambled eggs and cook together, season with turmeric/pepper/salt, top with avocado and nutritional yeast.

Macros: Protein 22g | Healthy fats 28g | Carbs 18g (12g net) | Fiber 6g | ~420 kcal. Delivers Vitamin D, B12, B6, Biotin, Folate, C, E, K2, plus Magnesium, Selenium, Potassium, Iron, Copper, Manganese. Blood sugar impact: low — stable 4-5 hours.

title: Enhanced Breakfast: Omega-3 Overnight Oats with Superfoods
body:
½ cup rolled oats (gluten-free) + 1 tbsp chia seeds + 1 tbsp ground flaxseeds + 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds + ½ cup fortified unsweetened almond milk + ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt + ¼ cup blueberries + 1 tsp cinnamon + 5 chopped walnut halves.

Method: mix oats, chia, flax and pumpkin seeds in a jar; stir in almond milk and yogurt; add cinnamon; refrigerate overnight (6+ hours); top with blueberries and walnuts in the morning.

Macros: Protein 18g | Healthy fats 22g | Carbs 42g (30g net) | Fiber 12g | ~410 kcal. Delivers Vitamin D, B1, B12, C, E plus Magnesium, Zinc, Calcium, Iron, Manganese, Copper, Phosphorus. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate, stable 4-5 hours.

title: Enhanced Breakfast: Savory Moong Dal Chilla
body:
½ cup moong dal (soaked 4-6 hours) + 1 tbsp nutritional yeast + ½ cup grated vegetables (zucchini, carrot) + 1 tsp each cumin/coriander/turmeric + 1 tsp grass-fed ghee + fresh cilantro.

Method: grind soaked dal into a smooth batter with minimal water, mix in yeast/vegetables/spices, cook thin like a pancake in ghee on a non-stick pan until golden on both sides (2-3 min/side), garnish with cilantro.

Macros: Protein 20g | Healthy fats 8g | Carbs 38g (30g net) | Fiber 8g | ~310 kcal. Delivers B1, B6, B9, B12, C, E, K, K2 plus Magnesium, Iron, Potassium, Zinc. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate.

title: Enhanced Breakfast: Greek Yogurt Power Bowl
body:
1 cup plain Greek yogurt + 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds + 2 tbsp sunflower seeds + 1 tbsp chia seeds + ¼ cup sliced strawberries + 5 chopped walnut halves + 1 tsp raw honey (optional, minimal) + a pinch of cinnamon.

Method: layer everything on top of the yogurt in a bowl.

Macros: Protein 25g | Healthy fats 24g | Carbs 28g (22g net) | Fiber 6g | ~420 kcal. Delivers B12, C, E, B1, B6 plus Magnesium, Zinc, Calcium, Iron, Selenium. Blood sugar impact: low, stable 4-5 hours.

title: Enhanced Breakfast: Avocado & Egg Power Toast
body:
1 slice whole grain (sprouted preferred) bread + ½ avocado mashed + 2 boiled or poached eggs + a handful of fresh spinach + 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds + a pinch of chili flakes, lemon juice and sea salt.

Method: lightly toast the bread, mash avocado with lemon/salt/chili and spread on top, layer spinach, top with the eggs, sprinkle pumpkin seeds.

Macros: Protein 18g | Healthy fats 26g | Carbs 30g (22g net) | Fiber 8g | ~420 kcal. Delivers Vitamin D, B12, Biotin, E, Folate, K2 plus Magnesium, Zinc, Selenium, Potassium. Blood sugar impact: low, 4-5 hour energy.

title: Enhanced Lunch: Wild-Caught Salmon with Quinoa & Greens
body:
100g wild-caught salmon + ½ cup cooked quinoa + 1 cup steamed broccoli + ½ cup sautéed spinach + 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon, garlic, parsley/dill.

Method: marinate salmon in lemon/olive oil/garlic/herbs, bake or grill at 180°C for 15-18 min; cook quinoa (1:2 water ratio, simmer 15 min); steam broccoli 5 min; sauté spinach with garlic 2 min. Serve salmon over quinoa with the vegetables, drizzle olive oil and lemon.

Macros: Protein 35g | Healthy fats 20g | Carbs 32g (26g net) | Fiber 6g | ~460 kcal. Delivers Vitamin D, B12, C, E, K, Folate, B1, B6 plus Omega-3, Magnesium, Selenium, Iron, Chromium, Manganese, Phosphorus. Blood sugar impact: low, stable 5-6 hours.

title: Enhanced Lunch: Chickpea & Veggie Stir-Fry with Tahini
body:
1 cup boiled chickpeas + 1 cup mixed vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, carrot, spinach) + 1 tbsp sesame oil + 1 tbsp tahini + garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric + fresh lemon juice.

Method: sauté garlic/ginger in sesame oil 1 min, add vegetables and stir-fry 5 min, add chickpeas and spices, cook 3 min, drizzle tahini and lemon before serving.

Macros: Protein 16g | Healthy fats 14g | Carbs 42g (32g net) | Fiber 10g | ~360 kcal. Delivers B6, Folate, C, E plus Magnesium, Iron, Zinc, Calcium, Copper, Potassium. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate.

title: Enhanced Lunch: Paneer Tikka with Rainbow Salad
body:
100g paneer cubes + 1 tbsp plain yogurt + turmeric/cumin/chili powder/lemon/garlic marinade + 2 cups mixed salad (cucumber, tomato, lettuce, bell pepper, red cabbage) + 1 tbsp olive oil dressing + 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds.

Method: marinate paneer 30 min, grill or bake at 180°C for 15 min until golden; toss the salad with olive oil, lemon, salt and pepper, top with pumpkin seeds; serve alongside the paneer.

Macros: Protein 22g | Healthy fats 18g | Carbs 16g (12g net) | Fiber 4g | ~320 kcal. Delivers B12, C, E, Folate plus Calcium, Magnesium, Zinc, Potassium. Blood sugar impact: low, stable 4-5 hours.

title: Enhanced Lunch: Lentil & Spinach Soup (Dal Palak) with Ghee
body:
½ cup masoor dal + 2 cups fresh spinach + 1 chopped tomato + garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, coriander + 1 tsp grass-fed ghee + fresh lemon juice.

Method: pressure-cook the dal with turmeric (3 whistles); separately temper cumin seeds in ghee, add garlic/ginger, then tomato until soft, then spinach until wilted; mix into the cooked dal, simmer 5 min, finish with lemon.

Macros: Protein 18g | Healthy fats 6g | Carbs 40g (32g net) | Fiber 8g | ~290 kcal. Delivers B1, B6, B9, C, E, K2 plus Magnesium, Iron, Potassium. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate.

title: Enhanced Lunch: Brown Rice Power Bowl with Egg & Avocado
body:
½ cup cooked brown rice + 2 boiled eggs (sliced) + ½ avocado (sliced) + 1 cup sautéed vegetables (bell pepper, broccoli, carrot) + 1 tbsp sesame seeds + low-sodium soy sauce, ginger, garlic.

Method: cook rice (1:2.5 water ratio, simmer 40 min); sauté vegetables with garlic/ginger 5 min; assemble rice as the base, top with vegetables, egg and avocado, drizzle soy sauce, sprinkle sesame seeds.

Macros: Protein 18g | Healthy fats 22g | Carbs 45g (38g net) | Fiber 7g | ~450 kcal. Delivers Vitamin D, B12, B1, B6, Biotin, E, Folate, K2, C plus Magnesium, Selenium, Potassium, Calcium, Copper, Manganese, Chromium. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate.

title: Enhanced Dinner: Baked Chicken with Roasted Rainbow Vegetables
body:
100g chicken breast + 1 cup mixed vegetables (zucchini, bell pepper, carrot, broccoli) + 1 tbsp olive oil + rosemary, garlic, thyme, black pepper + lemon.

Method: marinate chicken in olive oil/rosemary/garlic/lemon 15 min; lay chicken and chopped vegetables on a tray, drizzle oil, season, bake at 180°C for 25-30 min; serve with a lemon wedge.

Macros: Protein 30g | Healthy fats 16g | Carbs 18g (14g net) | Fiber 4g | ~340 kcal. Delivers B6, B12, C, E, Niacin plus Selenium, Chromium, Potassium. Blood sugar impact: low, stable overnight.

title: Enhanced Dinner: Palak Paneer with Whole Wheat Roti
body:
100g paneer + 2 cups spinach + 1 tomato + garlic, ginger, cumin, garam masala, turmeric + 1 whole wheat roti + 1 tsp grass-fed ghee.

Method: blanch spinach 1 min and blend into a smooth paste; temper cumin in ghee, sauté garlic/ginger, add tomato until soft, stir in the spinach paste and spices, add paneer cubes, simmer 5 min; serve with the roti.

Macros: Protein 20g | Healthy fats 16g | Carbs 30g (24g net) | Fiber 6g | ~350 kcal. Delivers B12, C, E, Folate, B1, K2 plus Magnesium, Calcium, Iron. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate, stable overnight.

title: Enhanced Dinner: Moong Dal Khichdi with Ghee & Vegetables
body:
¼ cup moong dal + ¼ cup brown rice + 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, beans) + 1 tsp grass-fed ghee + cumin, turmeric, ginger, asafoetida.

Method: pressure-cook the dal, rice and vegetables with turmeric (3 whistles); temper cumin in ghee with ginger and asafoetida, pour over the khichdi and mix well; serve warm.

Macros: Protein 14g | Healthy fats 6g | Carbs 48g (40g net) | Fiber 8g | ~310 kcal. Delivers B1, B6, B9, C, E, K2 plus Magnesium, Manganese. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate — easy to digest, ideal for dinner.

title: Enhanced Dinner: Grilled Mackerel with Sautéed Greens
body:
100g mackerel (or salmon/sardines) + 2 cups mixed greens (spinach, methi, kale) + 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon, garlic, black pepper, herbs.

Method: marinate fish in lemon/garlic/olive oil/herbs 15 min, grill or bake at 180°C for 12-15 min; sauté greens with garlic 3 min; serve together with a squeeze of fresh lemon.

Macros: Protein 28g | Healthy fats 24g | Carbs 10g (8g net) | Fiber 2g | ~370 kcal. Delivers Omega-3, Vitamin D, B12, E, Folate plus Magnesium, Selenium, Iron. Blood sugar impact: low — anti-inflammatory dinner.

title: Enhanced Dinner: Stuffed Bell Peppers (Vegetarian)
body:
2 large bell peppers + ½ cup cooked quinoa + ½ cup black beans + ½ cup diced tomatoes + 1 tbsp olive oil + cumin, paprika, garlic powder, turmeric + fresh cilantro.

Method: cut the tops off the peppers and remove seeds; mix quinoa, beans, tomatoes and spices; stuff into the peppers, drizzle olive oil, bake at 180°C for 25 min; garnish with cilantro.

Macros: Protein 14g | Healthy fats 10g | Carbs 46g (36g net) | Fiber 10g | ~330 kcal. Delivers C, E, B1, B6, Folate plus Magnesium, Iron, Potassium, Manganese. Blood sugar impact: low-moderate — high fiber, ideal for dinner.

title: UrCare Reversal Meal List — The Formula
body:
A large recipe database for diabetes reversal: High Fiber • High Protein • Low Carb • Moderate Fat, with vegetarian and non-vegetarian recipes kept separate.

The formula for every meal: 50% high fiber (leafy greens, cruciferous vegetables, seeds), 30% high protein (eggs, lean meats, paneer, tofu, sprouts), 20% healthy fat (ghee, olive oil, nuts — in moderation). Low carb throughout: no sugar, no white rice, no wheat flour — replaced with almond, coconut, besan or chickpea flour.

Usage: vegetarians can choose any breakfast recipe #1-20, non-vegetarians #1-40; rotate different meals through the week; one recipe = one serving; eat breakfast within 1-2 hours of waking.

title: Shopping List — Core Essentials
body:
Proteins (veg): paneer, tofu, soya chunks/granules, besan, moong dal, unsweetened Greek yogurt. Proteins (non-veg): eggs, chicken breast/thighs, fish, prawns, chicken sausages, turkey/chicken slices, canned tuna, canned sardines.

High-fiber vegetables (buy weekly) — leafy: spinach, methi, lettuce, coriander; crunchy: capsicum, cucumber, broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage; volume: bottle gourd, ridge gourd, pumpkin, eggplant, mushrooms, zucchini.

Fats & pantry: ghee, olive oil, coconut oil, butter; nuts/seeds — almonds, walnuts, chia, flaxseed, pumpkin seed, sunflower seed, peanuts; low-carb flours — almond, coconut, besan, oat, ragi; spices — turmeric, cumin, coriander powder, garam masala, pink/black salt, black pepper, mustard seeds, curry leaves, ajwain, cardamom, chaat masala, pav bhaji masala; others — psyllium husk (isabgol), green chili, ginger, garlic, lemon, stevia, low-sodium soy sauce, sugar-free tamarind chutney.

title: Meal List Breakfast #1 (Veg): Paneer & Flaxseed Cheela
body:
Ingredients: 100g grated paneer, 3 tbsp besan, 2 tbsp flaxseed powder, 1 chopped green chili, 2 tbsp coriander, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt, water as needed, 1 tsp ghee/olive oil.

Method: mix paneer, besan and flaxseed powder with the chili, coriander, turmeric and salt; add water to a thick dosa-like batter; cook thin on a ghee-greased tawa, 2-3 minutes per side until golden.

Macros (per serving): 410 kcal | Protein 23g | Net Carbs 9g | Fiber 8g | Fats 30g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #2 (Veg): Almond Flour & Spinach Roti
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup almond flour, 2 tbsp psyllium husk, ¼ cup blanched spinach puree, ½ tsp ajwain, salt, warm water as needed, 1 tbsp ghee.

Method: knead almond flour, psyllium husk, spinach puree, ajwain and salt with warm water into a soft dough; rest 5 minutes; pat into rotis between plastic sheets and cook on a tawa with ghee until lightly browned both sides.

Macros (per batch, ~4 rotis): 720 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 24g | Fats 62g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #3 (Veg): Sprouted Moong & Pomegranate Bowl
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup sprouted moong (steamed 5 min), ¼ cup pomegranate seeds, ½ diced cucumber, ½ tsp chaat masala, a pinch of black salt, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander.

Method: mix steamed sprouts with cucumber and pomegranate, season with chaat masala, black salt and lemon, garnish with coriander; serve chilled or at room temperature.

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 12g | Net Carbs 28g | Fiber 10g | Fats 1g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #4 (Veg): Tofu Bhurji
body:
Ingredients: 200g crumbled firm tofu, 1 chopped onion, 1 chopped tomato, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp pav bhaji masala, ½ tsp cumin seeds, salt, 1 tbsp olive oil, coriander.

Method: temper cumin in oil, sauté onion till translucent, add tomato till soft, stir in turmeric and pav bhaji masala, add crumbled tofu and cook 5 minutes, garnish with coriander.

Macros (per serving): 310 kcal | Protein 34g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 6g | Fats 18g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #5 (Veg): Greek Yogurt Parfait
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup unsweetened Greek yogurt, 2 tbsp chia seeds, 8-10 chopped walnuts, ¼ tsp cinnamon, 2-3 drops stevia (optional).

Method: layer yogurt, chia seeds and walnuts in a bowl, dust with cinnamon, add stevia if desired, let sit 5 minutes and serve chilled.

Macros (per serving): 380 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 9g | Fiber 11g | Fats 24g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #6 (Veg): Methi & Besan Pola
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup finely chopped fresh methi leaves, ½ cup besan, 2 tbsp curd, 1 tsp ginger paste, 1 chopped green chili, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt, water as needed, 2 tsp ghee.

Method: mix besan, curd, methi, ginger, chili, turmeric and salt into a thick batter, rest 10 minutes; cook small pancakes on a covered pan to steam the methi (2 min), flip and finish uncovered, apply ghee.

Macros (per serving): 280 kcal | Protein 14g | Net Carbs 24g | Fiber 7g | Fats 12g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #7 (Veg): Mushroom & Cheese Sauté
body:
Ingredients: 200g sliced button mushrooms, 3-4 minced garlic cloves, 1 tbsp butter, 1 cheese slice, ½ tsp oregano, ½ tsp black pepper, salt.

Method: sauté garlic in butter 30 seconds, add mushrooms and cook on high heat 4-5 minutes until the water evaporates, season, top with the cheese slice while hot until it melts.

Macros (per serving): 210 kcal | Protein 11g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 2g | Fats 17g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #8 (Veg): Soya Granules Upma
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup soya granules (soaked in hot water 10 min, squeezed dry), 1 tsp mustard seeds, 8-10 curry leaves, ¼ cup each chopped beans and carrot, 1 slit green chili, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt, 1 tbsp olive oil, coriander.

Method: temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and chili in oil, add beans/carrot and sauté 3 minutes, add turmeric/salt and the squeezed soya granules, cover and steam 5 minutes on low heat, garnish.

Macros (per serving): 290 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 14g | Fiber 11g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #9 (Veg): Coconut Flour Porridge
body:
Ingredients: 3 tbsp coconut flour, 1 cup unsweetened almond milk, ¼ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds, 2-3 drops stevia (optional), a pinch of salt.

Method: heat almond milk, whisk in coconut flour gradually, add cardamom and salt, cook 2 minutes until thick, sweeten if desired, top with pumpkin seeds.

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 7g | Net Carbs 6g | Fiber 10g | Fats 11g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #10 (Veg): Palak Paneer Cutlets
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup blanched, squeezed and chopped spinach, 100g grated paneer, 2 tbsp oat flour (binder), 1 tsp ginger paste, 1 chopped green chili, ¼ tsp garam masala, salt, 2 tbsp olive oil.

Method: mix spinach, paneer, oat flour, ginger, chili, garam masala and salt, shape into cutlets, shallow-fry 3 minutes per side until golden; serve with green chutney.

Macros (per serving): 490 kcal | Protein 22g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 4g | Fats 40g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #11 (Veg): Chia Seed Pudding (Saffron)
body:
Ingredients: 3 tbsp chia seeds, 1 cup unsweetened coconut milk, 8-10 saffron strands, 3-4 drops stevia, 1 tbsp chopped almonds.

Method: stir chia seeds into coconut milk with saffron and stevia, refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours), top with chopped almonds before serving.

Macros (per serving): 280 kcal | Protein 7g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 12g | Fats 23g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #12 (Veg): Vegetable & Paneer Stir-fry
body:
Ingredients: 150g cubed paneer, ½ each red/yellow/green capsicum (cubed), ½ cubed zucchini, 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame seeds, 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper.

Method: toss paneer in hot oil 1 minute until slightly golden, add capsicum and zucchini and toss on high heat 3-4 minutes (keep crunchy), add soy sauce/salt/pepper, finish with sesame seeds.

Macros (per serving): 580 kcal | Protein 30g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 5g | Fats 46g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #13 (Veg): Avocado & Cottage Cheese Mash
body:
Ingredients: 1 ripe avocado, 100g crumbled paneer/cottage cheese, 1 tbsp lemon juice, ¼ tsp chili flakes, salt, 1 thick-sliced cucumber for serving.

Method: mash the avocado with the paneer, lemon juice, chili flakes and salt (keep slightly chunky), top thick cucumber rounds with the mash.

Macros (per serving): 540 kcal | Protein 21g | Net Carbs 9g | Fiber 14g | Fats 46g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #14 (Veg): Roasted Chana Chaat
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup skinless roasted chana, 1 small chopped onion and tomato, 2 tbsp grated raw mango, 2 tbsp coriander, ½ tsp chaat masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp green chutney (optional).

Method: toss the roasted chana with onion, tomato, raw mango and coriander, season with chaat masala, lemon and chutney, let sit 2 minutes and serve.

Macros (per serving): 360 kcal | Protein 19g | Net Carbs 45g | Fiber 14g | Fats 6g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #15 (Veg): Ragi & Curd Smoothie
body:
Ingredients: 2 tbsp ragi flour, ½ cup water, 1 cup buttermilk/thin curd, ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, salt, coriander.

Method: cook ragi flour with water into a lump-free thick paste (3-4 min), cool completely, blend with buttermilk, cumin powder and salt, garnish and drink.

Macros (per serving): 160 kcal | Protein 10g | Net Carbs 22g | Fiber 3g | Fats 3g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #16 (Veg): Broccoli & Almond Tikki
body:
Ingredients: 2 cups grated broccoli, 3 tbsp almond powder, 2 tbsp grated cheese, 1 chopped green chili, ¼ tsp black pepper, salt, 2 tbsp olive oil.

Method: mix broccoli, almond powder, cheese, chili, pepper and salt into a patty mix, shape into tikkis, pan-fry 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

Macros (per serving): 380 kcal | Protein 13g | Net Carbs 8g | Fiber 6g | Fats 33g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #17 (Veg): Green Pea & Mint Mash
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup boiled green peas, ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 garlic cloves, ¼ tsp black pepper, salt.

Method: boil peas until soft, drain, roughly mash with mint, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, pepper and salt; serve warm.

Macros (per serving): 250 kcal | Protein 8g | Net Carbs 16g | Fiber 7g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #18 (Veg): Pumpkin Seed & Berry Bowl
body:
Ingredients: 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds, 1 tbsp sunflower seeds, 1 cup unsweetened Greek yogurt, 4-5 sliced strawberries, ¼ tsp vanilla extract (optional).

Method: mix vanilla into the yogurt, stir in the seeds, top with sliced strawberries and serve immediately.

Macros (per serving): 310 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 3g | Fats 16g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #19 (Veg): Cauliflower Poha
body:
Ingredients: 2 cups grated cauliflower, 2 tbsp peanuts, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 8-10 curry leaves, ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 chopped green chili, 1 tbsp lemon juice, salt, 1 tbsp olive oil, coriander.

Method: temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and peanuts in oil, add chili, cauliflower, turmeric and salt, cover and cook on low heat 5-7 minutes, finish with lemon juice and coriander.

Macros (per serving): 260 kcal | Protein 9g | Net Carbs 10g | Fiber 6g | Fats 20g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #20 (Veg): Masala Peanuts & Veggies
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup pressure-cooked (boiled) peanuts, ½ each chopped onion/tomato/cucumber, ½ tsp chaat masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander, salt.

Method: pressure-cook peanuts 10 minutes, cool, toss with the chopped vegetables, chaat masala, lemon juice, salt and coriander; serve immediately.

Macros (per serving): 350 kcal | Protein 15g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 8g | Fats 25g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #21 (Non-Veg): Masala Omelette with Spinach
body:
Ingredients: 2 whole eggs, ½ cup chopped spinach, 1 small chopped onion, 1 chopped green chili, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt and pepper, 1 tsp olive oil/butter.

Method: whisk eggs with the vegetables and spices, cook in a hot pan 2 minutes, flip and finish 1-2 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 210 kcal | Protein 13g | Net Carbs 4g | Fiber 1g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #22 (Non-Veg): Boiled Egg Chaat
body:
Ingredients: 2 diced boiled eggs, ¼ chopped onion and tomato, 1 tbsp sugar-free tamarind chutney, 1 tsp green chutney, ½ tsp chaat masala, 1 tbsp sev (optional, minimal), coriander.

Method: toss the diced eggs with onion, tomato, chutneys and chaat masala, top with a little sev and coriander.

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 13g | Net Carbs 6g | Fiber 1g | Fats 10g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #23 (Non-Veg): Chicken Sausages & Mushrooms
body:
Ingredients: 2 low-starch chicken sausages, 1 cup sliced mushrooms, ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp mixed herbs, salt, 1 tsp olive oil.

Method: pan-fry sliced sausages 2 minutes, add mushrooms, pepper, herbs and salt, toss and cook 4-5 minutes until tender.

Macros (per serving): 250 kcal | Protein 18g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 1g | Fats 17g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #24 (Non-Veg): Scrambled Eggs with Broccoli
body:
Ingredients: 2 whole eggs, 1 cup small broccoli florets, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 tbsp butter, salt and pepper.

Method: sauté garlic in butter, add broccoli 3-4 minutes, pour in whisked eggs and scramble 2 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 280 kcal | Protein 16g | Net Carbs 4g | Fiber 2g | Fats 22g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #25 (Non-Veg): Egg White Muffins
body:
Ingredients: 6 egg whites, ¼ cup each chopped bell pepper and spinach, 2 tbsp grated cheese (optional), salt, pepper, olive oil spray.

Method: whisk egg whites, fold in vegetables/cheese/seasoning, pour into a greased muffin tray and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 150 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 3g | Fiber 1g | Fats 3g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #26 (Non-Veg): Poached Eggs on Tomato
body:
Ingredients: 2 eggs, 1 large tomato (thick slices), ½ tsp oregano, salt and pepper, 1 tsp olive oil.

Method: sear tomato slices in oil 2 minutes per side with seasoning, poach or fry the eggs, place one on each tomato slice and serve.

Macros (per serving): 200 kcal | Protein 13g | Net Carbs 4g | Fiber 1g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #27 (Non-Veg): Chicken Keema (Breakfast Style)
body:
Ingredients: 200g minced chicken, 1 tsp ginger paste, ¼ cup green peas, 1 small chopped onion, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp garam masala, salt, 1 tsp olive oil, coriander.

Method: sauté onion and ginger, add minced chicken and dry-fry 5 minutes, add peas and spices, cook 5 more minutes until dry.

Macros (per serving): 360 kcal | Protein 44g | Net Carbs 8g | Fiber 3g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #28 (Non-Veg): Smoked Salmon/Fish & Cucumber
body:
Ingredients: 100g smoked salmon or steamed fish, 1 cucumber (thick sticks), 2 tbsp cream cheese, 1 tsp lemon juice, black pepper.

Method: spread cream cheese (mixed with lemon and pepper) on cucumber sticks, wrap with fish, secure with a toothpick, serve chilled.

Macros (per serving): 240 kcal | Protein 22g | Net Carbs 4g | Fiber 1g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #29 (Non-Veg): Egg Bhurji with Capsicum
body:
Ingredients: 2 whole eggs, ½ chopped capsicum, 1 small chopped onion, ½ tsp pav bhaji masala, ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 green chili, salt, 1 tsp butter/ghee.

Method: sauté onion, capsicum and chili 2 minutes, add turmeric and masala, crack eggs directly into the pan and scramble until done.

Macros (per serving): 220 kcal | Protein 13g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 1g | Fats 16g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #30 (Non-Veg): Turkey Slices with Avocado
body:
Ingredients: 4-5 deli turkey/chicken breast slices, ½ ripe avocado, black pepper, lemon juice.

Method: slice avocado into strips, season with pepper and lemon, roll a strip inside each turkey slice, secure with a toothpick, serve cold.

Macros (per serving): 280 kcal | Protein 24g | Net Carbs 3g | Fiber 5g | Fats 17g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #31 (Non-Veg): Shakshuka (Indian Style)
body:
Ingredients: 2 eggs, 1 medium chopped onion and tomato, 1 tsp cumin seeds, ¼ tsp red chili powder, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt, 1 tbsp olive oil, coriander.

Method: cook onion/tomato with spices into a gravy (5 min), make two wells, crack in the eggs, cover and steam 4-5 minutes, garnish and serve.

Macros (per serving): 310 kcal | Protein 14g | Net Carbs 9g | Fiber 2g | Fats 23g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #32 (Non-Veg): Fish Cutlets (Oat Crusted)
body:
Ingredients: 200g steamed and mashed fish, 1 tsp ginger paste, 1 chopped green chili, 2 tbsp oat flour (in the mix) + 2 tbsp for coating, ¼ tsp garam masala, salt, 2 tbsp olive oil.

Method: mix mashed fish with ginger, chili, oat flour, masala and salt, shape into cutlets, coat with oat flour and pan-fry 3 minutes per side until golden.

Macros (per serving): 420 kcal | Protein 42g | Net Carbs 14g | Fiber 2g | Fats 20g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #33 (Non-Veg): Anda Ghotala (Surat Style)
body:
Ingredients: 1 grated boiled egg + 1 raw egg, 1 small chopped onion and tomato, 1 tsp pav bhaji masala, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt, 1 tsp butter, coriander.

Method: sauté onion/tomato with spices, stir in the grated boiled egg, crack in the raw egg and scramble 2 minutes, garnish and serve.

Macros (per serving): 220 kcal | Protein 14g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 1g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #34 (Non-Veg): Prawn & Spring Onion Stir-fry
body:
Ingredients: 200g cleaned small prawns, ½ cup chopped spring onion, 3 minced garlic cloves, 1 tbsp soy sauce, ¼ tsp black pepper, salt, 1 tbsp olive oil.

Method: toss garlic in hot oil, add prawns and stir-fry 2 minutes on high heat, add spring onion/soy sauce/seasoning, toss 1 more minute until prawns turn pink.

Macros (per serving): 310 kcal | Protein 42g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 1g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #35 (Non-Veg): Chicken Liver Fry (Pepper)
body:
Ingredients: 200g cleaned chicken liver, 1 tbsp coarsely crushed black pepper, 10-12 curry leaves, 1 sliced onion, ½ tsp turmeric, salt, 1 tbsp ghee.

Method: sauté curry leaves and onion in ghee until golden, add turmeric and liver pieces, cook on high heat 5-6 minutes, finish with crushed pepper and salt.

Macros (per serving): 410 kcal | Protein 36g | Net Carbs 9g | Fiber 1g | Fats 23g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #36 (Non-Veg): Egg & Cheese Roll-up
body:
Ingredients: 1 whole egg, 1 cheese slice, 1 tsp butter, salt, pepper, oregano.

Method: make a thin omelette, place the cheese slice in the centre, fold into a roll and let the cheese melt.

Macros (per serving): 190 kcal | Protein 11g | Net Carbs 1g | Fiber 0g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #37 (Non-Veg): Tuna Salad Bowl
body:
Ingredients: 1 can tuna in water (drained), 1 tsp mayonnaise, ½ cup chopped lettuce, ¼ diced cucumber, 1 tbsp lemon juice, salt and pepper.

Method: mix drained tuna with mayonnaise, toss in lettuce, cucumber, lemon juice, salt and pepper; serve chilled.

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 2g | Fiber 1g | Fats 6g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #38 (Non-Veg): Sardines on Cucumber Toast
body:
Ingredients: 1 can sardines (water or olive oil), 1 cucumber (thick rounds), 1 tbsp lemon juice, black pepper, oregano.

Method: top thick cucumber rounds with sardine chunks, drizzle lemon juice and sprinkle pepper/oregano, serve chilled.

Macros (per serving): 220 kcal | Protein 24g | Net Carbs 4g | Fiber 1g | Fats 12g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #39 (Non-Veg): Mug Omelette (Microwave)
body:
Ingredients: 2 eggs, 2 tbsp chopped peppers, 1 tbsp grated cheese, salt, pepper.

Method: whisk everything in a microwave-safe mug, microwave on high 90 seconds (add 30 more if needed until set).

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 14g | Net Carbs 2g | Fiber 0g | Fats 12g.

title: Meal List Breakfast #40 (Non-Veg): Chicken Salami & Cheese
body:
Ingredients: 8-10 low-starch chicken salami slices, 8-10 cheese cubes, 8-10 pitted olives, toothpicks, black pepper.

Method: thread a cheese cube and olive onto a toothpick, wrap with a salami slice and secure, sprinkle pepper; serve as finger food.

Macros (per serving): 350 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 4g | Fiber 1g | Fats 26g.

title: Meal List Lunch #41 (Veg): Palak Paneer (No Cream)
body:
Ingredients: 200g cubed paneer, 2 cups fresh spinach, 4-5 garlic cloves, 1 green chili, 2 tbsp yogurt, ½ tsp cumin seeds, ¼ tsp garam masala, salt, 1 tbsp ghee.

Method: blanch spinach and blend with garlic/chili into a puree; temper cumin in ghee, add the puree and cook 3-4 minutes, stir in yogurt/salt/garam masala, add paneer and simmer 5 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 350 kcal | Protein 20g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 3g | Fats 28g.

title: Meal List Lunch #42 (Veg): Bharwa Karela (Stuffed Bitter Gourd)
body:
Ingredients: 4 medium karela, 1 large finely chopped onion, 2 tsp coarsely crushed fennel seeds, 1 tsp amchur, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, salt, 3 tbsp mustard oil.

Method: slit karela lengthwise, salt and rest 30 minutes then squeeze out bitterness; stuff with the spiced onion mix; cook covered in mustard oil on low heat, turning every 5 minutes, for 20-25 minutes until soft.

Macros (per serving): 220 kcal | Protein 4g | Net Carbs 10g | Fiber 6g | Fats 21g.

title: Meal List Lunch #43 (Veg): Soya Chunk Curry
body:
Ingredients: 1.5 cups soaked soya chunks (squeezed dry), 1 small cubed potato (optional, minimal), 1 large chopped onion, 2 pureed tomatoes, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chili powder, salt, 2 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: brown the onion, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato puree, cook the spices in 5 minutes, add soya chunks/potato and water, pressure cook 2 whistles (or simmer covered 15 minutes).

Macros (per serving): 280 kcal | Protein 25g | Net Carbs 15g | Fiber 8g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Lunch #44 (Veg): Bhindi Masala (Dry)
body:
Ingredients: 300g dried, slit okra, 1 large sliced onion, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp amchur, salt, 2 tbsp oil.

Method: temper cumin, fry onion until golden, add okra and let it cook undisturbed 3 minutes, then stir in turmeric/coriander/salt and cook 15-20 minutes on medium-high until crisp, finish with amchur.

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 3g | Net Carbs 8g | Fiber 5g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #45 (Veg): Rajma with Cauliflower Rice
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup soaked kidney beans, 2 pureed tomatoes, 1 chopped onion, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp rajma masala, ½ tsp turmeric, salt, 1 tbsp oil, 2 cups grated cauliflower, ½ tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp ghee.

Method: pressure-cook the soaked beans (4-5 whistles); separately brown onion, add ginger-garlic paste/tomato/spices, add the cooked beans and simmer 10 minutes, mashing some for thickness; sauté grated cauliflower with cumin in ghee 5-7 minutes and serve the rajma over it.

Macros (per serving): 350 kcal | Protein 15g | Net Carbs 25g | Fiber 14g | Fats 12g.

title: Meal List Lunch #46 (Veg): Methi Malai Paneer (Cashew Cream)
body:
Ingredients: 200g cubed paneer, 2 cups chopped fresh methi leaves, 3 tbsp cashew paste, 1 onion (paste), 1 tsp ginger paste, ½ tsp kasuri methi, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp garam masala, salt, 2 tbsp oil.

Method: brown the onion paste in oil, add ginger and turmeric, add blanched methi and sauté 3 minutes, stir in cashew paste and a little water for a white gravy, add paneer/kasuri methi/garam masala/salt and simmer 5 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 380 kcal | Protein 21g | Net Carbs 6g | Fiber 2g | Fats 30g.

title: Meal List Lunch #47 (Veg): Baingan Bharta
body:
Ingredients: 1 large eggplant (500g), 1 large chopped onion, 1 chopped tomato, 4-5 chopped garlic cloves, 1 chopped green chili, ½ tsp cumin seeds, ¼ tsp turmeric, coriander, salt, 2 tbsp mustard oil.

Method: char-roast the eggplant directly on a flame until soft, peel and mash; temper cumin and garlic in hot mustard oil, add onion until soft, then chili/tomato until soft, stir in turmeric/salt and the mashed eggplant, cook 5-7 minutes, garnish.

Macros (per serving): 170 kcal | Protein 3g | Net Carbs 10g | Fiber 7g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #48 (Veg): Mixed Vegetable Korma
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup chopped beans, 1 cup cubed carrot, ½ cup green peas, 1 cup cauliflower florets, ½ cup coconut milk, 1 onion (paste), 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, ½ tsp garam masala, 4-5 ground cashews, 2 cloves, 1 bay leaf, salt, 2 tbsp oil.

Method: steam the vegetables to 70% doneness; brown onion paste with the whole spices, add ginger-garlic, then cashew paste, steamed vegetables, coconut milk, salt and garam masala, simmer 5-7 minutes until creamy.

Macros (per serving): 280 kcal | Protein 5g | Net Carbs 14g | Fiber 6g | Fats 22g.

title: Meal List Lunch #49 (Veg): Dal Tadka (Thick)
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup toor or moong dal, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 chopped tomato, salt, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 4-5 sliced garlic cloves, 2 dry red chilies, curry leaves, coriander.

Method: pressure-cook the dal with turmeric (3 whistles), mash lightly, add tomato and salt and simmer 5 minutes (keep thick); temper cumin, garlic, chilies and curry leaves in ghee and pour over the dal as tadka, garnish.

Macros (per serving): 260 kcal | Protein 12g | Net Carbs 25g | Fiber 10g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #50 (Veg): Tofu Kadai
body:
Ingredients: 200g cubed firm tofu (pressed), capsicum and onion cut into strips, 1 chopped tomato, 2 tsp kadai masala, 1 tsp julienned ginger, ½ tsp turmeric, salt, 2 tbsp oil, kasuri methi.

Method: shallow-fry the tofu until golden and set aside; sauté ginger and onion, add capsicum, tomato, kadai masala and turmeric, cook 3-4 minutes on high heat, return the tofu with salt and crushed kasuri methi, toss 2 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 220 kcal | Protein 16g | Net Carbs 8g | Fiber 4g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #51 (Veg): Lauki Chana Dal
body:
Ingredients: 2 cups peeled, cubed bottle gourd, ½ cup soaked chana dal, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 slit green chili, salt, 1 tsp ghee, ½ tsp cumin seeds, a pinch of hing, curry leaves.

Method: pressure-cook the dal, gourd, turmeric, chili and salt with water (3 whistles), mash lightly; temper cumin, hing and curry leaves in ghee and pour over as a finishing tadka.

Macros (per serving): 190 kcal | Protein 9g | Net Carbs 20g | Fiber 8g | Fats 7g.

title: Meal List Lunch #52 (Veg): Mushroom Masala
body:
Ingredients: 300g halved button mushrooms, 1 large onion (paste), 2 pureed tomatoes, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp kasuri methi, salt, 2 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: brown onion paste, add ginger-garlic then tomato puree and spices, cook 5-6 minutes, add mushrooms and cook covered 5 minutes until the gravy thickens, finish with garam masala and crushed kasuri methi.

Macros (per serving): 160 kcal | Protein 5g | Net Carbs 8g | Fiber 3g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #53 (Veg): Chole Salad Bowl
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup boiled chickpeas, diced cucumber/tomato/onion/½ capsicum, 2 tbsp tahini or lemon juice, 1 tsp chaat masala, ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, salt, coriander.

Method: boil and cool the chickpeas, toss with the diced vegetables, tahini/lemon, chaat masala, cumin and salt, garnish and serve chilled or at room temperature.

Macros (per serving): 240 kcal | Protein 10g | Net Carbs 20g | Fiber 9g | Fats 12g.

title: Meal List Lunch #54 (Veg): Gobi Aloo (Low Aloo)
body:
Ingredients: 3 cups cauliflower florets (80%), 1 small cubed potato (20%), 1 tsp ginger paste, 1 chopped green chili, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp cumin seeds, salt, 2 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: temper cumin/ginger/chili in oil, sauté the potato 2 minutes, add cauliflower with turmeric/coriander/salt and a little water, cover and steam-cook on low heat 12-15 minutes until tender.

Macros (per serving): 180 kcal | Protein 4g | Net Carbs 12g | Fiber 5g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #55 (Veg): Black Chana Curry
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup soaked black chickpeas (kala chana), 2 pureed tomatoes, 1 chopped onion, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp amchur, salt, 2 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: pressure-cook the soaked chana until soft (5-6 whistles); brown onion, add ginger-garlic/tomato/spices and cook the masala 5 minutes, add the chana and simmer 10-12 minutes with amchur until thick.

Macros (per serving): 290 kcal | Protein 13g | Net Carbs 25g | Fiber 12g | Fats 15g.

title: Meal List Lunch #56 (Veg): Paneer Jalfrezi
body:
Ingredients: 200g paneer, capsicum and onion cut into strips, 2 diced tomatoes, 2 tbsp sugar-free tomato sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, ½ tsp black pepper, salt, 2 tbsp oil.

Method: lightly fry paneer strips and set aside, sauté ginger-garlic/onion/capsicum on high heat, add tomatoes/sauce/vinegar/pepper/salt, toss the paneer back in for 2 minutes.

Macros (per serving): 340 kcal | Protein 19g | Net Carbs 8g | Fiber 3g | Fats 26g.

title: Meal List Lunch #57 (Veg): Lobia (Black-Eyed Peas) Curry
body:
Ingredients: 1 cup soaked lobia, 2 pureed tomatoes, 1 chopped onion, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp turmeric, salt, 2 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: pressure-cook the soaked lobia (3 whistles); brown onion, add ginger-garlic/tomato/turmeric/coriander, add the lobia with some cooking water and simmer 8-10 minutes, finish with garam masala.

Macros (per serving): 270 kcal | Protein 14g | Net Carbs 24g | Fiber 11g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #58 (Veg): Zucchini Noodles with Pesto
body:
Ingredients: 2 large zucchini, 1 cup fresh basil, ¼ cup walnuts, 3-4 garlic cloves, 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp grated parmesan, salt and pepper.

Method: blend basil, walnuts, garlic, parmesan, olive oil, salt and pepper into a pesto; spiralize the zucchini into noodles (raw or lightly sautéed 2 minutes to keep crunchy), toss with the pesto.

Macros (per serving): 250 kcal | Protein 6g | Net Carbs 5g | Fiber 3g | Fats 23g.

title: Meal List Lunch #59 (Veg): Sprouted Moong Curry
body:
Ingredients: 1.5 cups sprouted moong, 1 chopped onion, 1 chopped tomato, 1 tsp ginger paste, 1 tsp goda/garam masala, ½ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp cumin seeds, salt, 2 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: steam the sprouts lightly 5 minutes; temper cumin, sauté onion, add ginger/tomato/turmeric/masala 3 minutes, add the sprouts with water and salt, simmer 10 minutes to a medium consistency.

Macros (per serving): 210 kcal | Protein 10g | Net Carbs 18g | Fiber 6g | Fats 14g.

title: Meal List Lunch #60 (Veg): Turai (Ridge Gourd) Sabzi
body:
Ingredients: 3 medium peeled, cubed ridge gourd, 4-5 chopped garlic cloves, 2 slit green chilies, ½ tsp cumin seeds, ¼ tsp turmeric, salt, 1 tbsp oil, coriander.

Method: temper cumin/garlic/chili in oil, add the ridge gourd with turmeric and salt, cover and cook on low heat 15-20 minutes (it releases its own water) until very soft.

Macros (per serving): 90 kcal | Protein 2g | Net Carbs 6g | Fiber 4g | Fats 7g.
